accepted.question_text: Let the vertices of the complete graph K_m be linearly ordered and identified with {1,2,...,m}. Two independent edges ij and st are called nested when i < s < t < j or s < i < j < t. Determine the smallest integer m such that every 2-coloring of the edges of this ordered complete graph contains a monochromatic non-nested matching of size n.

evidence.quote: Let us order the vertices of a complete graph K_m and identify the vertices with the set {1, 2, . . . , m}. Two independent edges ij and st are nested, if i < s < t < j or s < i < j < t. If we 2-color the edges, then we would like to find a large monochromatic non-nested matching. Problem 1.1 Determine the smallest m such that in every 2-coloring of the edges of the ordered complete graph K_m, there is a monochromatic non-nested matching of size n.

accepted.question_text: Consider a random 4-regular graph G defined as the union of two uniformly random cycles on the same vertex set. Is G also a.a.s. 3-choosable, meaning that G is properly colorable for every assignment of lists of three allowed colors to its vertices?

evidence.quote: Let us consider a random 4-regular graph G, defined as the union of two uniformly random cycles on the same vertex set. Such a graph G is a.a.s. 3-colorable [3], but it is an open question whether G is also a.a.s. 3-choosable, i.e., properly colorable for all assignments of lists of three allowed colors to vertices.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a random 4-regular graph, and let P_G = product over all edges uv in E(G) of (u - v), where the variables correspond to the vertices of G. In this 4-regular setting, the only relevant monomial for the Alon-Tarsi method is the product over all vertices v in V(G) of v^2. Is it true that the coefficient of P_G at that monomial is a.a.s. non-zero?

evidence.quote: A natural approach to resolving this is by using the Alon-Tarsi method [1]: Consider the graph polynomial P_G = Q_{uv in E(G)} (u-v) of a graph G, whose variables correspond to the vertices of G.

Note that the graph polynomial P_G is uniform and every monomial which appears in it with a non-zero coefficient has the same total degree, equal to |E(G)|. Hence, in our (4-regular) setting, the only relevant monomial is Q_{v in V(G)} v^2. Problem 2.1 Let G be a random 4-regular graph. Is it true that the coefficient of P_G at Q_{v in V(G)} v^2 is a.a.s. non-zero?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1 Let G be a disjoint union of cycles. Let H be a disjoint union of K_4's. Is G union H 4-colourable?

accepted.question_text: A strong edge coloring assigns colors to the edges of a graph so that any two edges that are adjacent or adjacent to a common edge receive distinct colors; equivalently, it is a proper coloring of the square of the line graph. Let chi'_s(G) denote the smallest number of colors in such a coloring. Diamond-free claw-free cubic graphs can be obtained from cubic graphs by truncation, meaning that each vertex is replaced by a triangle, and T(G) denotes the cubic graph obtained by truncating a cubic graph G. Is every diamond-free claw-free cubic graph strongly 6-edge-colorable? Equivalently, is chi'_s(T(G)) = 6 for every cubic graph G?
accepted.context_brief: Strong edge coloring of truncated cubic graphs

evidence.quote: A strong edge coloring assigns colors to the edges of a given graph in a way that any two edges that are either adjacent to each other or adjacent to a common edge receive distinct colors. In other words, it is a proper (vertex) coloring of the square of the line graph of a given graph. The smallest k such that a given graph G has a strong edge coloring with k colors is called the strong chromatic index of G and is denoted by chi'_s(G).

It is a well-known fact that diamond-free claw-free cubic graphs can be obtained from cubic graphs by the operation of truncation - replacing each vertex by a triangle. Let us denote T(G) the cubic graph obtained by truncating a cubic graph G. Problem 4.1 Is it true that every diamond-free claw-free cubic graph is strongly 6-edge-colorable? In other words, is it true that chi'_s(T(G)) = 6 for every cubic graph G?

accepted.question_text: A proper vertex coloring is called a 2-homogeneous coloring when exactly 2 colors appear in the open neighborhood of every vertex. If a cubic graph admits a 2-homogeneous coloring, are 4 colors always sufficient?
accepted.context_brief: Color bound for 2-homogeneous colorings of cubic graphs

evidence.quote: A proper coloring of vertices where in the open neighborhood of every vertex exactly k colors appear is k-homogeneous coloring [1].
Problem 5.1 If a cubic graph admits a 2-homogeneous coloring, then 4 colors are always sufficient.

accepted.question_text: Let G = (V, E) be a directed graph, let A be a non-trivial Abelian group, and let f map E into A. The boundary of f is the map partial f from V to A defined by partial f(x) = sum of f(e) over edges leaving x minus the sum of f(e) over edges entering x. The graph G is called A-connected if for every map b: V -> A with total sum 0 there exists a map f: E -> A - {0} such that b = partial f; an A-nowhere-zero-flow is such an f with partial f = 0. A graph is called almost-A-connected when all boundaries are admissible except partial f = 0. A snark is a cubic non-3-edge-colorable cyclically 4-edge-connected graph with girth at least 5, and it is bicritical if removing any two distinct vertices produces a 3-edge-colorable graph. Is every bicritical snark almost-Z_2^2-connected and almost-Z_4-connected?

evidence.quote: Let G = (V, E) be a directed graph, and f a mapping from E into a non-trivial Abelian group A. Associate with f its boundary partial f, a mapping from V to A, defined by partial f(x) = sum_{e leaving x} f(e) - sum_{e entering x} f(e). We say that G is A-connected if for every b : V -> A with sum_{x in V} b(x) = 0 there is an f : E -> A - {0} with b = partial f (and we call all these boundaries admissible).
An A-nowhere-zero-flow in G is such an f with partial f = 0.

Interestingly enough, by exhaustive search it's possible to show that for the Petersen graph all boundaries are admissible except for partial f = 0, both for Z_2^2 and Z_4 groups. We will call such graphs almost-A-connected graphs.

Looking at bigger examples of class 2 cubic graphs, a natural subfamily of graphs emerges known as snarks, which we define as cubic non-3-edge-colourable cyclically 4-edge-connected graphs with girth at least 5.
Problem 7.1 Every bicritical snark is almost-Z_2^2-connected and almost-Z_4-connected. A snark is bicritical [3] if the removal of any two distinct vertices produces a 3-edge-colourable graph.
